papers.title: AnySleep: a channel-agnostic deep learning system for high-resolution sleep staging in multi-center cohorts.
papers.summary: Developed AnySleep, a channel-agnostic deep neural network trained and validated on over 20,000 overnight recordings from 28 datasets that scores sleep from EEG or EOG at adjustable temporal resolution. It attains state-of-the-art 30-s epoch performance, remains strong with single EEG derivations or EOG alone, and at sub-30-s resolution captures short wake intrusions and improves prediction of obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy type 1, and insomnia.

papers.title: Reduced Locomotor Activity in Juvenile ICR and BALB/c Mice Exposed to Early-Life Sleep Restriction.
papers.summary: Juvenile ICR and BALB/c mice subjected to daily gentle-handling sleep restriction from postnatal day 8 to 21 showed reduced open-field locomotor activity in both strains, persisting to 8 weeks of age, while body weight and central-area exploration changes were strain-specific (ICR only). The authors conclude early-life sleep restriction reduces locomotor activity across genetic backgrounds, though handling stress could not be excluded.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment as a multisystem modulator of neurotransmitter function: mechanisms, plasticity, and therapeutic implications.
papers.summary: This structured narrative review (143 articles) synthesizes preclinical evidence that environmental enrichment modulates serotonergic, dopaminergic, glutamatergic, and GABAergic pathways, with weaker evidence for adrenergic and histaminergic systems, converging on receptor/transporter changes, neurotrophic signaling, CREB transcription, and epigenetic remodeling. Enrichment was consistently associated with enhanced neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity, stress resilience, and improved behavioral/cognitive outcomes.

papers.title: Decoding Parkinson's disease: a systematic review of qEEG biomarkers across clinical domains.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 89 qEEG studies in Parkinson's disease found spectral slowing (reduced posterior dominant frequency, increased theta) was the most consistent correlate of cognitive impairment, while connectivity measures (PLV, graph metrics) showed stronger associations with motor dysfunction, gait impairment, and freezing; qEEG also changed with dopaminergic drugs, neuromodulation, and spindle density reductions linked to dementia risk.

papers.title: An automated EEG-ECG framework for CAP-HRV analysis: enabling brain-heart coupling studies in sleep disorders.
papers.summary: Presents an open-source MATLAB framework integrating rule-based CAP A1 detection during slow-wave sleep with HRV feature extraction via PhysioZoo/mhrv in a single time-synchronized EEG-ECG pipeline. A worked example on the OSAD+ subgroup (n=18) and a descriptive healthy-sleep A1-event HRV reference from the CAP Sleep Database (15 controls, 785 A1 epochs) demonstrate synchronized CAP-HRV output; CAP A1 detection is not yet benchmarked against expert manual scoring.

papers.title: Nocturnal intravenous gamma-hydroxybutyrate and sleep architecture in non-sedated intensive care unit patients: a polysomnographic experience.
papers.summary: A polysomnographic letter reporting the experience of nocturnal intravenous gamma-hydroxybutyrate and its effects on sleep architecture in non-sedated intensive care unit patients; the supplied record contains no abstract, so no specific findings can be stated.

papers.title: Differential circadian time modulates of dentate gyrus and CA1 excitation-inhibition balance and seizure threshold.
papers.summary: Using vEEG, optogenetic seizure induction, mRNA sequencing, and patch-clamp in male ICR mice, this study found divergent circadian regulation of seizure thresholds between dentate gyrus and CA1, with the CA1 diurnal-nocturnal pattern matching systemic pilocarpine-induced seizures. Circadian cycles differentially modulated excitatory/inhibitory synaptic transmission and intrinsic excitability of DG and CA1 principal neurons.

papers.title: Adjunctive Trazodone Effects on Sleep, Mood, and Circulating 5-HT and BDNF in Depression.
papers.summary: In this retrospective propensity-score-matched study of 156 depressed patients, adjunctive trazodone plus fluvoxamine versus fluvoxamine monotherapy reduced awake time, prolonged REM and slow-wave sleep, improved sleep quality and HAMD/HAMA scores at week 4, and increased circulating 5-HT and BDNF at week 8, with a higher overall clinical response rate.

papers.title: Validation of the Telephone MoCA in iRBD and Parkinson's Disease with Conversion to the Standard MoCA.
papers.summary: In 137 OPDC cohort participants (controls, iRBD, PD), T-MoCA and face-to-face MoCA-22 scores were statistically equivalent with minimal bias, though concordance was moderate (Lin's CCC=0.58). An equipercentile equating conversion from MoCA-22 to MoCA-30 was derived and externally validated across three cohorts totaling 14,375 assessments.

papers.title: Chronic circadian misalignment in military personnel: a potential contributor to neuroinflammation risk.
papers.summary: Reviews evidence proposing that chronic circadian misalignment in military personnel is a modifiable contributor to neuroinflammatory risk, acting through core clock gene disruption (CLOCK, BMAL1), mitochondrial and redox dysfunction, neuroimmune imbalance, and compromised synaptic plasticity and blood-brain barrier integrity. Argues this raises vulnerability to cognitive dysfunction and mood disturbances even in healthy, fit individuals, warranting targeted intervention and mechanistic study.

papers.title: A technical review of dynamic brain functional imaging combined with EEG spectral parameters in the screening of early-stage brain injury.
papers.summary: Proposes a Dynamic-Spectral Coupling (DSC) framework and narratively reviews dynamic fMRI, EEG spectral analysis (spectral slowing and 1/f aperiodic components), and multimodal fusion for screening early-stage brain injury such as mTBI, silent stroke, and subclinical injury. Summarizes screening value, translational limitations, and future directions including lightweight devices and AI-assisted diagnosis, while noting clinical utility remains to be established.

papers.title: Associations of self-reported physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep duration with mental and behavioral health among civil aviation flight students: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional survey of 776 civil aviation flight students (analyses restricted to 774 males) examining associations of self-reported physical activity intensity, sedentary time, and sleep duration with depression, anxiety, stress, and problematic Internet use using generalized estimating equation models. After FDR correction, sleep duration <7 h was associated with higher depression, anxiety, stress, and problematic Internet use scores, longer vigorous-intensity activity with lower anxiety, and longer sedentary time with higher problematic Internet use, with generally small effect sizes.

papers.title: Hair-compatible adhesive hydrogel electrodes for electroencephalography-based cybersickness detection and closed-loop mitigation.
papers.summary: Develops a shell-assisted adhesive hydrogel electrode, incorporating PEDOT-modified polydopamine particles, that penetrates hair and stably adheres to the scalp for rapid EEG acquisition, achieving an 11.66 dB SNR and motion interference under sweating at 22.8% of traditional wet electrodes. Integrated into a wearable headband, the system detected cybersickness with 92.5% accuracy and enabled closed-loop noisy galvanic vestibular stimulation that increased users' tolerance time by 52.3%.

papers.title: Automated attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder detection using an explainable EEGNet model based on electroencephalogram signals.
papers.summary: Developed a specialized, lightweight EEGNet deep learning model that processes raw 5-second spatio-temporal EEG segments for automated ADHD detection without manual feature engineering, achieving 89.48% average accuracy and 0.96 AUC and outperforming transfer learning models. Saliency maps and SHAP values identified key channels (Fp1, Fp2, C3, T5, A2) consistent with established ADHD neuroscience, supporting an interpretable assistive diagnostic framework.

papers.title: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with repeated experience sampling
papers.summary: This paper introduces a multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset in BIDS format from 24 healthy adults, including carbon wire loop sensors for artifact removal, continuous performance task responses, experience sampling of 13 thought dimensions, and mental health surveys across two days (~1.33 hours of simultaneous EEG-fMRI per individual). The dataset supports study of brain activity during wakeful rest and cross-session reliability of EEG-fMRI relationships.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine-related interventions and the cGAS-STING axis in neuroinflammation: disease contexts and mechanisms of action.
papers.summary: This review organizes preclinical evidence on how traditional Chinese medicine interventions (herbal formulas, natural compounds, acupuncture, electroacupuncture) modulate the cGAS-STING axis in neuroinflammation, stratified by disease context and site of action. It reports that modulation direction is context-sensitive: pathway-related inflammation is reduced in several sterile injury models, restored STING signaling accompanies protection in acute sleep deprivation and early HSV infection, and increased STING-IFN-I signaling accompanies electroacupuncture analgesia in pain models.

papers.title: Screen time exposure, sleep alterations, and their relationship with excess weight in children and adolescents.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 70 pediatric patients, obese children showed higher perivisceral fat, systolic blood pressure, insulin, and HOMA index and lower HDL cholesterol than non-obese peers. Obese children also had greater daily screen time (2.9 vs 2.1 h) and shorter sleep (8.4 vs 9.1 h), and screen time was associated with higher obesity risk after adjustment (OR 3.08).

papers.title: Co-exposure to octocrylene and polystyrene nanoplastics induces neuro- and reproductive toxicity in zebrafish: Association with circadian rhythm and HPG axis disruption.
papers.summary: Adult zebrafish were exposed for 28 days to octocrylene (5 µg/L) with or without 80 nm polystyrene nanoplastics (1.0 mg/L). Co-exposure aggravated neurotoxicity (altered behavior, suppressed bdnf, downregulated circadian clock genes) and reproductive toxicity via HPG-axis disruption, with molecular docking suggesting OC interaction with estrogen receptors and CYP19.

papers.title: Associations of circadian clock genes with the risk of depression in adults with sleep disturbances: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 studies examined circadian clock genes in adults with sleep disturbances and depression. Eight genes (CLOCK, NR1D, TIM, CRY, PER2, PER3, ARNTL, CSNK1) were associated with depression, with CRY showing the numerically highest pooled odds ratio (OR 1.6, 95% CI 1.4-1.8), while RORA was not significant.

papers.title: Impact of nocturnal oxygen saturation on sleep quality and exercise performance in adult Fontan patients.
papers.journal: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
authors: Kyle G P J M Boyle
papers.summary: Sixteen adult Fontan patients and 16 matched controls underwent actigraphy and nocturnal pulse oximetry over six nights plus cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Fontan patients had greater nocturnal desaturation (-3.4 vs -2.5 percentage points), longer sleep onset latency (22.8 vs 10.8 min), and lower self-perceived physical functioning, with nocturnal SpO2 indices related to daytime sleepiness and reduced exercise performance.

papers.title: Gray matter alterations and their atlas-based spatial associations with neurotransmitter distributions in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: Structural MRI in 109 patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder and 24 controls identified baseline gray matter volume changes (reduced right cerebellar cortex/vermis, increased left putamen/pallidum) spatially aligned with dopaminergic receptor and transporter maps. Phenoconverters had lower baseline right medial orbital gyrus volume, spatially correlated with serotonergic, glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic maps in exploratory analyses.

papers.title: Preoperative Sleep Modulation with Melatonin and Zolpidem and Its Impact on Postoperative Pain and Recovery: A Scoping Review.
papers.journal: Journal of pain & palliative care pharmacotherapy
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesized 16 studies on preoperative melatonin or zolpidem in surgical patients, finding that melatonin showed anxiolytic, analgesic, and chronobiotic effects (reducing salivary cortisol and modulating stress/inflammatory pathways) while zolpidem improved preoperative sleep quality and reduced postoperative pain and opioid consumption, with possible TNF-α reduction in colorectal surgery. The authors conclude the two agents offer complementary perioperative benefits and call for larger dosing and patient-selection trials.

papers.title: Insomnia and medication overuse headache: neurobiological links, reciprocal interactions, and integrated therapeutic strategies.
papers.summary: This narrative review examined the reciprocal relationship between insomnia and medication overuse headache, integrating Mendelian randomization, polysomnographic, withdrawal-trial, and neurobiological evidence to implicate orexinergic dysregulation, melatonin suppression, and glial neuroinflammation in a self-reinforcing cycle. It proposes that concurrent withdrawal, CBT-I, preventive pharmacotherapy including anti-CGRP antibodies, and CPAP where indicated may outperform sequential management, but notes this remains untested in randomized trials.

papers.title: Cortical traveling wave analysis reveals weaker resting forward theta waves and greater task-related modulation in obsessive compulsive disorder.
papers.summary: Using resting-state and task-based EEG in 25 OCD patients and 27 controls, this study quantified cortical traveling waves and found weaker resting forward (posterior-to-anterior) theta waves in OCD and greater task-related forward theta modulation during the Flanker task, with no symptom-severity correlations. The findings suggest disrupted hierarchical cortical communication and a potential trait-like neurophysiological marker of OCD.

papers.title: Unleashing children's potential: An evidence-based narrative review of strategies to enhance cognitive function and intelligence in school-age children.
papers.summary: This evidence-based narrative review synthesizes interventions—including nutrition, gut-brain interactions, physical activity, sleep, parenting, stress regulation, educational curricula, digital learning, mindfulness, and social-emotional learning—that can enhance cognitive function and executive function in school-age children (6-12 years), including special populations. It critically appraises methodological heterogeneity and translational gaps and proposes priorities for multimodal, personalized, scalable interventions.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm dysregulation and ferroptosis in hypertension: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
papers.summary: This review proposes a mechanistic model in which circadian disruption creates a temporal mismatch between oxidative stress generation and antioxidant defense, lowering the ferroptosis threshold in cardiovascular and renal tissues and thereby amplifying hemodynamic stress, endothelial dysfunction, impaired renal sodium handling, and hypertension progression. It highlights circadian-ferroptosis interplay as a potential therapeutic target while acknowledging limited direct causal evidence.

papers.title: Case Report: Electroencephalography-informed low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area in severe functional movement disorder.
papers.summary: A case report of a patient with severe functional movement disorder following occupational injury in whom EEG network analysis-guided low-frequency rTMS targeting the supplementary motor area, combined with staged visual-feedback rehabilitation, reduced tremors and improved gait speed, activities of daily living, and EEG network connectivity.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance in inflammatory bowel disease: clinical associations and gaps in care.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 204 adults with inflammatory bowel disease found that 76.5% reported poor sleep quality and 55.9% had clinically significant sleep disturbance, which was associated with active disease, higher perceived stress, and anxiety, while intermediate and morning chronotypes were protective. Despite high interest in sleep interventions, exposure to cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia was minimal (0.5%).

papers.title: Neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia: a prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 39 infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia, 13 of 26 assessed at 24 months (50%) showed sub-normative Bayley-4 performance in at least one domain despite only one having acute MRI-detected injury. Sub-normative performance was associated with higher postnatal base deficits and lactate levels and a trend toward less aEEG sleep-wake cycling.

papers.title: Almond shells as environmental enrichment for laying hens: Implications for welfare and egg quality.
papers.summary: In a commercial aviary study with 2,500 hens per pen, coarsely milled almond shells as environmental enrichment reduced fearfulness in the novel object test and comb pecking wounds at peak lay and reduced fear responses and free feathers at post-peak, with a trend toward lower serum corticosterone, without affecting internal or external egg quality.

papers.title: Human iEEG recordings during audiovisual speech violations support and extend predictive routing models
papers.summary: Recorded intracranial EEG from superior temporal and prefrontal/premotor areas of seven presurgical epilepsy patients during an audiovisual speech paradigm to test predictive routing. Superior temporal cortex showed increased high-gamma and decreased alpha-beta power to auditory deviance and the McGurk condition, while frontal regions showed alpha-beta decreases without a high-gamma prediction error signal, and theta carried a strong prediction error signal in the McGurk condition—supporting and extending predictive routing models for human predictive processing.

papers.title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine lowered 24-h hs-cTnT (170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L) and CK-MB, improved preoperative sleep quality, and reduced postoperative delirium incidence (14.3% vs 37.1%) without differing adverse events.

papers.title: Psychological support for depression and anxiety across chronic illness contexts: a comparative evaluation of three general-purpose AI chatbots.
papers.summary: Standardized simulated-patient benchmarking study comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao on 20 depression/anxiety scenarios across type 2 diabetes and chronic spontaneous urticaria, yielding 120 blinded-rated responses. Overall appropriateness differed across systems (90.0% ChatGPT, 75.0% Gemini, 55.0% Doubao meeting threshold), performance dropped for moderate presentations (58.3% appropriate) and CSU contextualization, and major safety errors occurred in 0%, 10.0%, and 15.0% of first-round responses respectively.

papers.title: Nocturnal sleep duration, clinical activity score, and thyroid functional remission after radioactive iodine therapy in Graves' disease with thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy.
papers.summary: Retrospective single-center cohort of 153 patients with Graves' disease and thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy examined whether pretreatment nocturnal sleep duration and Clinical Activity Score predict thyroid functional remission after radioactive iodine therapy. Longer sleep (OR 6.13 per hour) and lower CAS (OR 0.64 per point) were associated with remission in post-selection models, and no patient sleeping under 6 h achieved remission, but the authors describe these threshold effects as exploratory and requiring prospective validation.

papers.title: The Moderating Effect of Sleep Duration on the Association Between Chronic Disease and Health-Related Quality of Life in Middle-Aged Women.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional secondary analysis of 3062 middle-aged Korean women from the 2019 and 2021 KNHANES examined whether sleep duration moderates the association between number of chronic diseases and health-related quality of life. More chronic diseases were associated with lower HRQOL, and this negative association was stronger among women sleeping more than 9 h/day than in the 6-7 h/day reference group.

papers.title: Effectiveness Evaluation and Predictive Model Construction of Multi-modal Intervention Program Based on Psychological Resilience Theory in Perioperative Anxiety Management for Cataract Surgery.
papers.summary: Conducted a prospective randomized controlled trial in 120 cataract surgery patients comparing routine perioperative care with a psychological resilience theory-based multi-modal intervention, plus construction of an anxiety risk prediction model. The intervention produced greater reductions in STAI state anxiety (16.6 vs 9.6 points at 1 month), improved resilience, anxiety, sleep, physiological and pain outcomes, higher surgical cooperation, shorter recovery, and fewer complications (28.6% vs 56.1%), while the seven-factor prediction model achieved an AUC of 0.863.

papers.title: Avoiding Diagnostic Pitfalls in Facial Pain: A Case Report of Paroxysmal Hemicrania Initially Treated as Trigeminal Neuralgia.
papers.summary: Reports a 21-year-old man with two-year recurrent strictly unilateral facial pain initially treated as trigeminal neuralgia with carbamazepine without benefit; attack duration and frequency, absent triggers, and restlessness suggested a trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia. A 14-day indomethacin trial (up to 225 mg daily) produced no improvement, so the diagnosis was recorded as probable paroxysmal hemicrania, and verapamil 240 mg daily was followed by marked reduction and eventual resolution of headache days, though causality cannot be established from a single uncontrolled case.

papers.title: The gut microbiota-derived butyrate improves gestational glucose homeostasis through HDAC3 inhibition and epigenetic activation of the SCGN/GLP-1 axis.
papers.summary: Combining a nested case-control clinical cohort, a high-fat-diet/antibiotic GDM mouse model treated with Clostridium butyricum, enteroendocrine cell multi-omics, and HDAC3-haploinsufficient mice, this study showed that butyrate improves gestational glucose homeostasis by inhibiting intestinal HDAC3, increasing H3K27ac at the SCGN promoter, and potentiating SCGN/GLP-1 secretion. Serum butyrate and active GLP-1 were lower in women who developed GDM, and C. butyricum's metabolic benefits and SCGN upregulation were abolished in HDAC3-haploinsufficient mice.

papers.title: Night Shift Work and Self-Reported Health Problems Among Hospital Workers in Mogadishu, Somalia: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: A descriptive cross-sectional survey of 300 night-shift hospital workers in Mogadishu, Somalia, characterized shift patterns and self-reported health problems. High prevalences were reported for stress (78.7%), frequent fatigue (76.0%), sleep problems (71.3%), reduced concentration (68.7%), and burnout symptoms (58.0%), but the absence of a day-shift comparison group means causation by night shift work cannot be established.

papers.title: Association Between Dietary Vitamin Intake and Short Sleep Duration Among Adults in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of 2021-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) Data.
papers.summary: Used cross-sectional 2021-2023 NHANES data from 4,169 U.S. adults to examine associations between dietary vitamin intake per 1,000 kcal and short sleep duration (<7 hours). Higher intake of vitamins A (aOR=0.710), B6 (aOR=0.724), and K (aOR=0.815) was associated with lower odds of short sleep duration, with weaker inverse associations for several other vitamins and a direct association for vitamin B9.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
